parts.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB
parts.host_requirements: PCIe slot; board-partner dimensions vary; NVIDIA reference requirement is 600W system power and an appropriate PCIe/Gen5 power connector.
parts.software_stack: CUDA; llama.cpp CUDA; PyTorch and CUDA-compatible inference runtimes

performance_evidence.notes: Catalog entry uses official capacity/power specs only; do not infer tokens/sec from AI TOPS.

parts.plain_language: Current 16GB CUDA GPU worth tracking as a relatively compact local-LLM card; actual value depends heavily on live board-partner pricing.
parts.source_notes: NVIDIA lists a 16GB GDDR7 configuration, 448 GB/s memory bandwidth and 180W Total Graphics Power for the RTX 5060 Ti.

parts.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24GB
parts.host_requirements: PCIe 4.0 x16-class host; reference card power is 350W and NVIDIA specifies 750W required system power for its reference configuration.
parts.software_stack: CUDA; llama.cpp CUDA; PyTorch and CUDA-compatible inference runtimes

performance_evidence.notes: Track exact board condition, cooling and used-market history separately from the reference GPU identity.

parts.plain_language: Older but still important 24GB CUDA card whose used-market price can make it one of the most interesting larger-model GPU candidates despite high board power.
parts.source_notes: NVIDIA specifies 24GB GDDR6X, a 384-bit interface and 350W reference graphics-card power. Used-board condition is a separate market-risk signal.

parts.name: AMD Radeon RX 9070 16GB
parts.host_requirements: PCIe add-in-card host; AMD reference TBP is 220W and recommended PSU is 650W.
parts.software_stack: ROCm where supported; llama.cpp HIP/Vulkan; PyTorch ROCm

performance_evidence.notes: ROCm documentation identifies RX 9070 as an RDNA4/gfx1201 GPU; collect exact-runtime LLM measurements separately.

parts.plain_language: 16GB RDNA4 card with strong memory bandwidth that is worth sourcing when ROCm/Vulkan compatibility for the intended runtime is confirmed.
parts.source_notes: AMD publishes 16GB GDDR6, 640 GB/s memory bandwidth and 220W total board power for RX 9070; ROCm lists the GPU as gfx1201.

parts.name: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16GB
parts.host_requirements: PCIe add-in-card host; AMD reference TBP is 304W and recommended PSU is 750W.
parts.software_stack: ROCm where supported; llama.cpp HIP/Vulkan; PyTorch ROCm

performance_evidence.notes: ROCm documentation identifies RX 9070 XT as an RDNA4/gfx1201 GPU; do not convert gaming/AI specifications into tokens/sec.

parts.plain_language: Faster 16GB RDNA4 option to compare against the non-XT card, with a substantial board-power penalty that should matter in off-grid or always-on deployments.
parts.source_notes: AMD publishes 16GB GDDR6, 640 GB/s memory bandwidth and 304W total board power for RX 9070 XT.

parts.name: Intel Arc B580 12GB
parts.host_requirements: PCIe 4.0 x8 add-in card; board reference TBP is 190W; verify platform Resizable BAR/support and board-vendor PSU requirements.
parts.software_stack: oneAPI; Intel Extension for PyTorch where supported; llama.cpp SYCL/Vulkan; OpenVINO

performance_evidence.notes: Track real llama.cpp/SYCL/Vulkan results separately from Intel peak TOPS.

parts.plain_language: 12GB Battlemage card worth tracking as a budget GPU candidate, particularly when live pricing undercuts 16GB cards enough to offset the smaller VRAM pool.
parts.source_notes: Intel publishes 12GB GDDR6, 456 GB/s memory bandwidth and 190W TBP for the B580 reference GPU.

parts.name: Intel Arc A770 16GB
parts.host_requirements: PCIe 4.0 x16-class host; Intel reference TBP is 225W; verify Resizable BAR support and board-vendor power requirements.
parts.software_stack: oneAPI; Intel Extension for PyTorch; llama.cpp SYCL/Vulkan; OpenVINO

performance_evidence.notes: Intel lists oneAPI, OpenVINO and Intel Extension for PyTorch support; collect exact local-LLM runtime measurements separately.

parts.plain_language: Older 16GB Arc card that becomes interesting when discounted heavily, especially for buyers willing to validate SYCL/Vulkan software compatibility.
parts.source_notes: Intel specifies 16GB GDDR6, 560 GB/s bandwidth, 225W TBP, oneAPI/OpenVINO support and Intel Extension for PyTorch support.
